parse.title: 2026 national electoral calendar
parse.text:
For local elections, see 2026 local electoral calendar.

2026 national electoral calendar

2027 →

This national electoral calendar for 2026 lists the national and federal elections held, and scheduled to be held, in 2026 in all sovereign states and their dependent territories. By-elections are excluded, though national referendums are included. Specific dates are given where these are known.

January

[edit]
  • 11 January:
    • Benin, Parliament[1]
    • Myanmar, Parliament (2nd phase)[2]
  • 15 January: Uganda, President and Parliament[3]
  • 18 January: Portugal, President (1st round)[4][5]
  • 25 January: Myanmar, Parliament (3rd phase)[6]

February

[edit]
  • 1 February: Costa Rica, President and Parliament[7]
  • 6 February: Tokelau, Parliament[8]
  • 8 February:
    • Japan, House of Representatives[9]
    • Portugal, President (2nd round)[10]
    • Thailand, House of Representatives and Constitutional referendum[11]
  • 11 February: Barbados, House of Assembly[12]
  • 12 February: Bangladesh, Parliament and Constitutional referendum[13]
  • 22 February: Laos, Parliament[14]

March

[edit]
  • 5 March: Nepal, House of Representatives[15]
  • 8 March:
    • Colombia, House of Representatives and Senate[16]
    • Switzerland, Referendums[17]
  • 15 March:
    • Kazakhstan, Constitutional referendum[18]
    • North Korea, Parliament[19]
    • Republic of the Congo, President[20]
    • Vietnam, Parliament[21]
  • 22 March: Slovenia, National Assembly[22]
  • 22–23 March: Italy, Constitutional referendum[23]
  • 24 March: Denmark, Parliament[24]
  • 26 March: Faroe Islands, Parliament[25]

April

[edit]
  • 4 April: Maldives, Constitutional referendum[26]
  • 10 April: Djibouti, President[27]
  • 12 April:
    • Benin, President[28]
    • Hungary, Parliament[29]
  • 12–13 April: Peru, President (1st round), Chamber of Deputies and Senate[30]
  • 19 April: Bulgaria, Parliament[31]
  • 26 April: Central African Republic, National Assembly (second round)
  • 30 April: Antigua and Barbuda, House of Representatives[32]

May

[edit]
  • 2 May: Niue, Parliament[33]
  • 12 May: Bahamas, House of Assembly[34]
  • 17 May: Cape Verde, Parliament[35]
  • 24 May: Cyprus, Parliament[36]
  • 30 May: Malta, Parliament[37]
  • 31 May:
    • Colombia, President (1st round)[38]
    • Guinea, National Assembly[39]

June

[edit]
  • 1 June: Ethiopia, House of Peoples' Representatives[40]
  • 7 June:
    • Armenia, Parliament[41]
    • Jersey, Parliament
    • Kosovo, Parliament[42]
    • Peru, President (2nd round)
  • 14 June: Switzerland, Referendums[43]
  • 21 June: Colombia, President (2nd round)[44]
  • 28 June: New Caledonia, Parliament[45]

July

[edit]
  • 2 July: Algeria, People's National Assembly[46]
  • 4 July: Slovakia, Referendum
  • 19 July: São Tomé and Príncipe, President[47]

August

[edit]
  • 12 August: Cook Islands, Parliament[48]
  • 13 August: Zambia, President and Parliament[49]
  • 23 August: Kazakhstan, Kurultai[50]
  • 29 August: Iceland, Referendum[51]
  • 30 August: Guinea-Bissau, Constitutional referendum

September

[edit]
  • 13 September: Sweden, Parliament[52]
  • 18 September: South Ossetia, President[53]
  • 18–20 September: Russia, State Duma[54]
  • 23 September: Morocco, House of Representatives[55]
  • 24 September: Isle of Man, House of Keys[56]
  • 27 September:
    • São Tomé and Príncipe, Parliament[47]
    • Switzerland, Referendums

October

[edit]
  • 3 October: Latvia, Parliament[57]
  • 4 October:
    • Bosnia and Herzegovina, Presidency and House of Representatives[58]
    • Brazil, President (1st round), Chamber of Deputies and Senate[59]
  • 9–10 October: Czech Republic, Senate (1st round)[60]
  • 11 October: Slovenia, Referendums
  • 16–17 October: Czech Republic, Senate (2nd round)
  • 25 October:
    • Bulgaria, President[61]
    • Serbia, Parliament[62]
    • Brazil, President (2nd round)
  • 27 October: Israel, Knesset[63]

November

[edit]
  • 3 November: United States, House of Representatives and Senate[64]
  • 5 November: Grenada, Parliament
  • 7 November: New Zealand, Parliament[65]
  • 15 November: Cape Verde, President[35]
  • 29 November:
    • Spain, Senate and Congress of Deputies
    • Switzerland, Referendums

December

[edit]
  • 5 December: Gambia, President[66]
  • 9 December: Fiji, Constitutional referendum[67]
  • 13 December: Transnistria, President[68]
  • 22 December: South Sudan, President, Assembly and Council of States[69]
  • 25 December: Serbia, President

Indirect elections

[edit]
  • 3–8 March: Iran, Supreme Leader[70]
  • 16 March, 18 June, and 16 October: India, Council of States[71]
  • 22 March: North Korea, President of the State Affairs[72]
  • 23 March: Laos, President[73]
  • 30 March: Myanmar, President
  • 3 April: Myanmar, Vice President[74]
  • 7 April: Vietnam, President
  • 11 April: Iraq, President[75]
  • 11 August: Hungary, President
  • 20 August: Bangladesh, President
  • 2 September: Estonia, President[76]
  • 27 September: France, Senate (series 2)
  • 6 October: Kosovo, President[77]
  • 9 December: Switzerland, Federal Council[78][79]
